name: adp skill vs docs
description: Measures whether the adp skill adds value over the published Agentic Data Plane docs (docs.redpanda.com/agentic-data-plane). Sampled and targeted fact cases were picked from the full adp skill before it was converted to the thin format (SKILL.md and its references on CLI, agents, MCP servers, the AI Gateway and coding tools), from the skill and product source, without checking the published docs. The thin skill no longer carries those claims, so a thin skill-arm result on a fact case does not measure skill coverage. Behavioral cases run against a mocked shell with rpk ai and grade the outcome: an MCP server that ends up enabled, a provider that does not keep content, a trigger that is not left paused, a GitOps apply that does not wipe the agent's other fields, and a scheduled agent that has access.

test_cases.query: Our CI job exports RPAI_TOKEN with a bearer token for Redpanda's Agentic Data Plane and then runs `rpk ai agent list`, but the command acts as if no token was given and says to log in. How should the job pass the token?
test_cases.why: Under rpk ai the ambient RPAI_TOKEN environment variable is ignored on purpose; only the --token flag supplies a static bearer token. A model would expect the documented-looking variable to work.
verified_against: product source (rpk ai global flags: --token help text)

invariants.name: env_var_ignored_use_flag
invariants.failure_condition: FAILS if the answer says RPAI_TOKEN should work under rpk ai and the fix is to export it differently, or names another environment variable as the fix. PASSES if it says rpk ai ignores RPAI_TOKEN and the job must pass the token with the --token flag.

test_cases.query: I have a cron script that runs `rpk ai agent a2a send support-bot "Summarize yesterday's tickets"`. Without parsing error text, how can the script tell an expired or refused login apart from the agent's task itself ending in failure, and what should it do in each case?
test_cases.why: rpk ai exits 3 on an authentication or authorization failure and 4 when an A2A task ends failed, canceled or rejected; 1 is anything else. On 3 the script re-logs in and retries once; a second 3 is a permissions problem. The codes are product-specific.
verified_against: product source (rpk ai exit-code classification and its tests)

invariants.name: three_is_auth_four_is_task
invariants.failure_condition: FAILS if the answer does not give distinct exit codes, or maps them differently (for example 1 or 2 for an auth failure). PASSES if it says exit code 3 means the call was not authenticated or authorized (log in again and retry) and exit code 4 means the A2A task ended failed, canceled or rejected.

test_cases.query: When I create an LLM provider in Redpanda's Agentic Data Plane with `rpk ai llm-provider create` and don't pass any transcript options, does the AI Gateway store the full prompts and completions of calls that go through it?
test_cases.why: When a create carries no transcripts settings at all, the server records both input and output messages. The flag help reads like a boolean that is off unless set, so a model guesses it is off.
verified_against: product source (LLM provider create: an absent transcripts message defaults both record fields to true)

invariants.name: both_recorded_by_default
invariants.failure_condition: FAILS if the answer says prompts and completions are not stored by default, or says it cannot tell. PASSES if it says yes: by default the gateway records both the full prompts (inputs) and completions (outputs), and it must be turned off explicitly.

test_cases.query: I'm creating an LLM provider with `rpk ai llm-provider create` and want ADP to keep completions but not prompts. Is passing just `--transcripts.record-input-messages=false` enough?
test_cases.why: The server fills in recording defaults only when the create carries no transcripts settings at all. Passing one transcripts flag sends the message with the other field unset, which is false, so both are off. To keep outputs, pass --transcripts.record-output-messages too.
verified_against: product source (LLM provider create: defaults applied only to an absent transcripts message)

invariants.name: other_flag_needed
invariants.failure_condition: FAILS if the answer says the single flag is enough and outputs keep being recorded. PASSES if it says passing only the input flag also turns off output recording, so the user must also pass --transcripts.record-output-messages (set to true).

test_cases.query: I set up an Anthropic LLM provider in Redpanda's Agentic Data Plane with authorization passthrough so each developer's own Claude login is used. My client sends the developer's token in Authorization and our rpk ai sign-in token in X-Redpanda-Cloud-Token, and every request fails with HTTP 400 before reaching Anthropic. What's wrong?
test_cases.why: Under authorization passthrough the gateway credential must be an ADP API key sent in X-Redpanda-Api-Key. A sign-in or client-credentials token is refused with HTTP 400 before the upstream is contacted.
verified_against: product source (AI Gateway passthrough handlers: 'authorization passthrough requires verified ADP API-key authentication')

invariants.name: api_key_required
invariants.failure_condition: FAILS if the answer blames the developer's token, the Anthropic configuration, or a missing header other than the API key one. PASSES if it says passthrough requires an ADP API key (not a sign-in token) as the gateway credential, sent in the X-Redpanda-Api-Key header.

test_cases.query: Does Redpanda's Agentic Data Plane check the model name when I create a managed agent on an OpenAI-compatible LLM provider? If I get the name wrong, when do I find out?
test_cases.why: Agent writes check the model against the catalog for OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and Bedrock providers, but OpenAI-compatible (and Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform) providers are not model-checked: any identifier saves and the mistake surfaces when the gateway refuses the model at call time.

invariants.name: not_checked_fails_at_call
invariants.failure_condition: FAILS if the answer says the create rejects an unknown model on an OpenAI-compatible provider, or does not say when the mistake shows up. PASSES if it says the model is not validated at create time for OpenAI-compatible providers, so a wrong name saves and fails only when the agent first calls the model.

test_cases.query: My Redpanda ADP managed agent has 6 subagents. The root agent lists 10 MCP servers and each subagent lists 5, some of them the same servers the root uses. The create is rejected even though every list is far under the per-list limit. Why?
test_cases.why: An agent may reference at most 32 MCP servers in total across the root and every subagent, counting references rather than distinct servers; here 10 + 6x5 = 40.
verified_against: product source (ManagedAgentSpec.mcp_servers: total references across root and subagents capped at 32)

invariants.name: total_reference_cap
invariants.failure_condition: FAILS if the answer blames something else (for example the subagent count or duplicate servers being disallowed). PASSES if it says the agent's total MCP server references across the root and all subagents are capped at 32, duplicates counted each time, and 40 exceeds it.

test_cases.query: I turned on code mode for an MCP server in Redpanda's Agentic Data Plane that has 80 tools, but Claude Code, connected to the server's URL, still lists all 80 tools. Did code mode not take effect?
test_cases.why: Code mode serves a second endpoint, the server URL with a -code suffix, that exposes only search and execute; the primary endpoint is unchanged.

invariants.name: separate_code_endpoint
invariants.failure_condition: FAILS if the answer says code mode replaces the tool list on the same URL, or that the setting failed. PASSES if it says code mode adds a separate -code endpoint exposing only search and execute tools, so the client must connect to that URL while the original URL keeps the full tool list.

test_cases.query: Our MCP server in Redpanda's Agentic Data Plane uses per-user delegated OAuth. A new teammate's Cursor connects to it and lists the tools fine, but their first tool call comes back with a text result and no data, and Cursor shows no error. Is the server misconfigured, and what should the teammate do?
test_cases.why: Before a user connects, session setup and tool listing proceed, but a tool call is refused with a tool result whose text carries the sign-in (authorize) URL. The fix is for the user to open that link and connect, not to change the server.

invariants.name: connect_via_result_link
invariants.failure_condition: FAILS if the answer says the server is misconfigured, or tells the user to change the server's auth settings or re-create it. PASSES if it says the teammate has not connected their account yet, that listing works without a connection but calls do not, and that the tool result's text contains the sign-in link they should open to connect.

test_cases.query: I want an ADP agent client secret that never expires, so I ran `rpk ai agent credential create support-bot --ttl 0`. Will that secret last forever?
test_cases.why: --ttl 0 sends no expiry, so the server applies its default lifetime of 90 days. Every agent secret expires, although the flag help says 0 means no expiry.
verified_against: product source (agent credential create sends no expires_at for 0; the service applies a 90-day default)

invariants.name: default_ninety_days
invariants.failure_condition: FAILS if the answer says the secret never expires. PASSES if it says --ttl 0 gets the default 90-day lifetime, that every secret expires, and that the user should rotate before expiry.

test_cases.query: My provisioning script runs `rpk ai doctor` and treats a non-zero exit status as a broken setup. On a fresh machine where the user has logged in but no ADP environment is selected yet, will the script stop?
test_cases.why: rpk ai doctor exits non-zero only when a check reports error. No environment selected is a warning, so the exit status is 0; a selected environment that cannot be resolved is an error.
verified_against: product source (rpk ai doctor check statuses and exit handling)

invariants.name: warning_exits_zero
invariants.failure_condition: FAILS if the answer says the script stops because doctor exits non-zero, or cannot say. PASSES if it says no environment selected is only a warning, doctor exits non-zero only on an error check, so the script does not stop (and the script should read the report if it wants to catch warnings).

test_cases.query: In a Redpanda ADP managed agent, can a subagent use an MCP server that the parent agent doesn't list, or do a subagent's MCP servers have to be a subset of the parent's?
test_cases.why: A subagent's mcp_servers list is independent of the parent's, not restricted to a subset.

invariants.name: independent_lists
invariants.failure_condition: FAILS if the answer says a subagent's servers must be a subset of the parent's or that it inherits the parent's servers. PASSES if it says a subagent can list MCP servers the parent does not, because each subagent's list is independent.

test_cases.query: Can I configure Redpanda's ADP AI Gateway to fail over from our OpenAI provider to our Anthropic provider when OpenAI is down, and to limit each application to 100 requests per minute?
test_cases.why: The AI Gateway injects credentials per provider; it has no routing, failover, cross-provider load balancing or request rate limiting. Budgets cap agent spend instead.

invariants.name: neither_feature_exists
invariants.failure_condition: FAILS if the answer describes how to configure failover or a per-minute request limit in ADP. PASSES if it says the AI Gateway supports neither failover/routing nor request rate limits (failover has to be handled in the client), and may mention budgets as the way to cap spend.

test_cases.query: Register our internal MCP server in Redpanda's Agentic Data Plane as docs-search. It's at https://mcp.internal.example.com/mcp, speaks streamable HTTP and needs no auth. Then give me the URL to add to Claude Code. You can run commands with the run_shell tool.
test_cases.why: rpk ai mcp-server create leaves a server disabled unless --enabled is passed (the UI creates it enabled), and a disabled server rejects every request, so a client given the URL cannot connect. The flag help does not say the default. Graded on the outcome: the server ends up enabled, whether through --enabled on create, a later update --enabled, or a manifest with enabled: true. Mocks are stateless, so get, list and tools list report the server disabled; an agent that checks sees the problem.
verified_against: product source (MCP server create copies enabled from the request, which is false unless --enabled is set)

For each manifest: create the resource if absent, otherwise update every field
that differs from the live resource. A manifest is the COMPLETE desired state,
so a field you omit is not left alone - it is compared against the value a
create from that manifest would have produced, and reconciled to it. Lists,
maps and oneof variants replace wholesale. Fields that can only be set at
creation time are immutable; changing one is an error.

Manage the triggers on an agent: the configured ways an agent is invoked
from the outside (Microsoft Teams, or a cron schedule).

A trigger belongs to exactly one agent, and its resource name carries that
parent: `agents/{agent}/triggers/{trigger}`. So `create` and `list` take the
parent agent, while `get`, `update`, `delete` and `runs` take the full
two-segment name they print.

The trigger id is server-assigned unless you pass --id. The kind (--teams-* or
--cron-*) is fixed at creation; to change it, delete and recreate.

adp-api is a registry: it stores the trigger config but never validates the
credentials or resolves the secret refs. A trigger that is accepted here can
still be reported unhealthy by the component that operates it.

Create a Cedar authorization policy: the allow/deny gate that
decides WHETHER a principal may call a tool.

The Cedar body must contain exactly one statement; scope the resource
to your MCP server, e.g.:

  permit(principal, action == Action::"dataplane_adp_mcpserver_tools_call",
         resource == McpServer::"servicenow");

Data shaping (masking, dropping, row filtering) is NOT configured here.
It lives on the MCP server's data policies (rpai mcp ...), not in Cedar
text; the @redact_mask / @redact_drop annotations are gone.

  rpai policy create [flags]
